beats.say: Marketing, supply chain and finance each own their data.
One central team cannot keep up with all of them. It becomes a bottleneck.
beats.label: The problem
beats.head: The central team is a bottleneck

beats.say: But if every team does its own thing, nothing fits together.
beats.label: The other problem
beats.head: No rules = nothing fits

beats.say: The answer is in the middle. It is called a data mesh.
beats.label: Station 3.4 · Designing a data platform
beats.head: The data mesh

check.prompt: In a data mesh, who owns the data products of a domain?
check.why: Each domain owns its products. The central team owns the rules and the platform.

beats.say: Each shop runs itself. It knows its own products best.
beats.label: The shops
beats.head: Each shop runs itself

beats.say: But the mall gives every shop the same building, power and safety rules.
beats.label: The mall
beats.head: Same building, same rules

beats.say: In a mesh, each domain team owns its data products. That is the shop.
beats.label: Domains
beats.head: Domains own their data products

beats.say: A central team owns the standards and the platform. That is the mall.
beats.label: Central team
beats.head: Central team: rules and platform

beats.say: On Google Cloud, five blocks build it.
Cloud Storage is the lake. BigQuery is the warehouse. Dataplex organizes and governs.
beats.label: The platform · 1 of 2

beats.say: The catalog makes data searchable. And Analytics Hub shares it, without copies.
beats.label: The platform · 2 of 2

beats.say: One mapping to remember. A Dataplex lake is one domain.
beats.label: Remember
beats.head: One Dataplex lake = one domain

beats.say: The trap: one team that owns every dataset, when the story describes independent domains.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: One central team owning every dataset
